title: Galactic Conjunction
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 105, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, D. Jones, A. Riess et al.Acknowledgement: R. Colombari

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The spiral galaxy NGC 105 seems to be plowing edge-on into a long, thin neighbor. The collision is an illusion. The two only line up by chance on the sky, and the elongated galaxy lies much farther off and has drawn little attention from astronomers. NGC 105 itself is roughly 215 million light-years away in Pisces.
Chance alignments like this are common. The stars of a constellation sit at very different distances from Earth and only look like a group from our viewpoint.

Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 took these data as part of a large set of observations of nearby galaxies that hold both Cepheid variables and supernovae. One is a class of pulsating star and the other the explosive death of a massive star, but both have predictable luminosities. Comparing their real brightness with how bright they look gives a distance. Because NGC 105 contains both, astronomers can check the two methods against each other.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 observed NGC 105 in visible and near-infrared light, through filters from 350 nm to 1.6 μm. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Part of the data is near-infrared light, which the eye cannot see, and Hubble's long exposures reveal far fainter detail than any eye could.

explore: Distances to galaxies including NGC 105 went into measuring the rate at which the Universe expands, known as the Hubble constant. The result disagrees with the most widely accepted cosmological model, and the analysis puts the odds that measurement errors caused the mismatch at only 1 in a million. The source says this adds persuasive evidence that the standard model of cosmology is wrong or incomplete.
alt: A spiral galaxy seen nearly edge-on beside a thinner, elongated galaxy that appears to touch it.
